html:
The April Uprising was a revolt against Ottoman rule in April and May 1876, started in the town of Koprivshtitsa and centred in the Sredna Gora and Rhodope regions of Bulgaria.

It was poorly armed and crushed within weeks, mostly by irregular troops called bashi-bazouks. Thousands of Bulgarians were killed, and in the town of Batak most of the people were massacred in the church and around it. Reports by American and British journalists caused outrage in Europe, and the British politician William Gladstone wrote a pamphlet on the Bulgarian horrors. The poet Hristo Botev died leading a band that crossed the Danube to join it. The outrage helped lead to the Russo-Turkish War that freed Bulgaria the next year.
